paper.title: Cognitive Medium Access: Exploration, Exploitation and Competition

settings.name_in_paper: Single user--single channel cognitive medium access (non-parametric) (lower bound)
unmapped: Rewards are B times Bernoulli(theta_i) (B = bandwidth in bits)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that at each time slot, channel $i$ is free with probability $\theta_i$. ... the loss entailed by $\Gamma$ is given by L(\thetav;\Gamma)=\sum_{j=1}^TB\theta_{i^*}-\sum_{j=1}^{T}B\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i Pr{\Gamma(\Psi(j))=i}

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-channel cognitive user (sensing M <= N channels simultaneously)
unmapped: Action = any subset of exactly M of the N channels (multiple plays); reward = sum of B*Bernoulli of selected channels; comparator = top-M channels
settings.definition_quote: we assume the presence of only a single cognitive user capable of sensing, and subsequently utilizing, $M\leq N$ channels simultaneously. ... L(\thetav;\Gamma)=\sum_{j=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^MB\theta_{i}-\sum_{j=1}^{T}B\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i P\{i\in \mathcal{M}(j)\}

settings.name_in_paper: Multi user--single channel, known theta (symmetric distributed strategy vs centralized)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: theta is known; result is a static allocation/optimization loss as the number of users grows, no learning
unmapped: loss measured against centralized allocation as number of users K grows
settings.definition_quote: we first consider the case in which the values of $\thetav$ are known to all the cognitive users. ... the loss of the distributed protocol as compared with the centralized scheduling is L=BT\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i(1-p_i^*)^{K}

algorithms.name: Staying with the winner and switching from the loser rule (Gamma_SW)
Order-optimal single index strategy for multi-channel sensing (Rule 4, UCB-type index with M largest)

symbols.mu_2nd: free probability of the second-best channel theta_{i**}

source.label: lem:sw
source.quote: No matter what the switching rule is, $L(\thetav;\Gamma_{SW})\sim O(T)$.

results.notes: Paper's O uses Knuth's convention meaning Theta; the proof lower bounds the loss of any SW rule by an optimistic version with stationary-distribution loss linear in T. Recorded as Omega(T)-type lower bound for this algorithm class.

source.quote: Rule~\ref{rule:multisense} is asymptotically optimal and $L(\thetav,\Gamma)\sim O(\ln T).$

results.notes: Proof shows E[Y_i(T)] <= M(ceil(8 ln T/(theta_M-theta_i)^2) + sum 4 j^{-3}) for each non-top-M channel; constants depend on the instance. Paper's O is Knuth's (Theta-like), but proof only gives an upper bound; lower order claim relies on Anantharam et al.

bound.regime: number of users N -> infinity, number of channels fixed

symbols.Q: number of channels with theta_i > 0 (2 <= Q <= number of channels)

source.quote: Let $2\leq Q\leq N$ be the number of channels for which $\theta_i>0$. We have $p_i^*\rightarrow 1/Q$, and $L\rightarrow 0$ exponentially as $K$ increases, i.e., $$L\sim O(e^{-c_1K}),$$ where $c_1=\ln \frac{Q}{Q-1}$.

results.notes: Paper's K (number of cognitive users) mapped to canonical N; paper's N (channels) is K. Limit constant is BT sum theta_i. Loss vs centralized allocation, not learning regret.
